name: DailyLeft
subtitle: Monthly budget and allowance
summary: Set a budget and see what you can spend today, worked out from the money and days you have left

hero.hook: Set a budget and see what you can spend today, worked out from the money and days you have left
hero.shotAlt: The DailyLeft main screen in Korean. An amount shows in large numbers, with a bar, a one-line status and a calendar below.

sections.title: What you can spend today
body: Enter a monthly budget, and the money left is divided by the days left to show what you can spend each day. When you spend, the daily amount is worked out again. One line below tells you whether your pace is comfortable or tight. With a daily budget, what is left for today shows in large numbers.

sections.title: Choose the days that count
body: Every day counts by default. Turn on Count Weekdays Only to leave out weekends, plus Korean public holidays if your iPhone's region is South Korea. To leave out a day you won't spend, tap it in the calendar. With a monthly budget, the daily amount is then divided again over the days left. Past days in the calendar show what you spent.

sections.title: Set it up for your budget
body: By default it helps you stay within budget. If the money disappears when the period ends, as with welfare points or a grant, turn on Expires If Unspent, and it tells you to use it all in time. Choose the day your budget starts, from the 1st to the 28th. The money left also shows in Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets.

sections.title: Recording payments
body: You can add any payment by hand. If your iPhone's region is South Korea, you can also record card payments from messages. If card payments reach you by text message, you can set up a Shortcuts automation to record them without opening the app. If they come through a card app or KakaoTalk, paste the notice or enter the amount yourself. Enter a card's last 4 digits to record only that card's messages, or leave them empty to record payment messages from every card.
bullets: Shortcuts automation
Pasting a payment notice
Adding by hand

sections.title: When the balance is off
body: If the record and your real balance differ, tap the big number and enter the real amount. One Balance adjustment line records the difference, and your original transactions stay as they are.

a: Choose a monthly or daily budget, enter one amount, and tap Start. There is no account or login.

If you start a monthly budget partway through a period, enter the real amount left in the Money Left This Month field. If you leave it empty, the full budget is used. The period start day, Count weekdays only, Expires if unspent, payment notices and card last 4 digits are under More Options, and you can change them later in Settings.

Every day counts by default. If the money isn't for weekends, turn on Count Weekdays Only in Settings. Weekends are left out, plus public holidays if your iPhone's region is South Korea. To leave out a specific day, tap it in the calendar on the main screen. When the calendar is collapsed it shows only this week, so tap Expand Calendar to reach other weeks. You can't leave out past days.

For the South Korea region, public holidays for 2026 to 2028 are built into the app, and later years are added in app updates. 2028 was worked out from the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute calendar data and will be checked again once the official dates are published. In years not on the list, only weekends are left out. Tap any temporary holiday that isn't on the list to leave it out in the calendar.

faq.q: Money left at the end of a period
a: Money left does not carry over to the next period. When a period ends, the budget starts again.
If the money disappears when unspent, as with welfare points or a grant, turn on Expires If Unspent in Settings. The app then tells you to use it all within the period.

faq.q: Daily budgets and the period start day
a: To budget by the day, change the budget type in Settings to Daily Budget. A new share appears on each counted day, and days that don't count have no share.
If your budget doesn't start on the 1st, pick a day from the 1st to the 28th in Period Start Day in Settings.

faq.q: The daily amount on a day you pay
a: With a monthly budget, if today is a counted day and you have a payment today, today's count ends and the money left is divided again from tomorrow. The screen shows Done for today. If you cancel every payment that day, today counts again. Balance adjustments don't count as payments.

faq.q: Recording text messages with a Shortcuts automation (South Korea)
a: This works only if your iPhone's region was South Korea when you first set up the app. Elsewhere, use Add by Hand. If payment notices reach you by text message, you can set up a Shortcuts automation. Open the app once, then open Build It Yourself under Shortcuts Automation in Settings to see the steps. The app action to add to the automation is called Record Payment Message. The steps follow the iOS 27 screens.

The app can't read your Messages directly. It reads only text passed by the automation or text you paste. The automation's Contains field decides which messages are passed. With only 승인 (approved) there, cancellation messages may not be recorded. To catch those too, put your card's last 4 digits in that field.

faq.q: Card app notices and KakaoTalk notices
a: iOS limits mean the app can't read card app notices or KakaoTalk notices automatically. Copy the notice and paste it into Add from Message, or use Add by Hand. Add from Message appears only for the South Korea region.

If you enter them, only messages from the card with those last 4 digits are recorded. If you leave them empty, payment messages from every card are recorded. In that case, messages with a readable date, time and amount are recorded, and messages containing the Korean words for deposit, withdrawal, transfer, loan, billing or statement are not recorded. Messages containing the Korean words for declined, failed, not possible, insufficient balance or over the limit count as declined and are never recorded, with or without the card digits.

faq.q: If a message isn't recorded (South Korea)
a: Check that the automation's Message Text field holds the trigger's Message. If you entered your card's last 4 digits, a message must show those 4 digits in full to be read. For other messages, empty the card field or use Add by Hand.

Messages are read using the Hana Card format as the base, and other card companies' messages are read by finding the amount, date and last 4 digits. Messages with no date or time can't be read, and payments not in won are not recorded.

If Add from Message can't read a message, Report Message appears under the result. Tap it to open a mail draft with the original text. You can delete or change the name, merchant or card number before sending. You send it yourself from your own mail app.
Reported messages are used only to teach the app that format and to reply to you.

Tap the big number or Adjust Balance and enter the real amount. One Balance adjustment line records the difference, and your original transactions stay as they are. Swipe in the list to delete adjustment lines and transactions.
To enter a cancellation or refund by hand, turn on Cancellation or Refund in Add by Hand.
Home Screen widgets come in small and medium sizes. They show the money left and what you can spend today, and the medium size also lists your 2 latest transactions.

There are three Lock Screen widgets. The rectangular one shows the money left and what you can spend today, the circular one shows the share left, and the inline one shows the money left. Until you enter a budget in the app, they show Not set up or a question mark.
Ads appear in one banner spot at the bottom of the main screen.

iOS asks whether to allow tracking after you tap Start on the first-run screen. You can use the app the same way if you don't allow it, and you can change this choice in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.
Where ad consent is required, such as the European Economic Area, the consent form appears before the tracking prompt. In those places you can change your consent from Privacy Choices in Settings.
Budget calculations, recording and widgets work without a connection. Ads, sending a report email and opening the privacy policy need a connection.
The app does not use iCloud sync, so records don't move to a new device by themselves.

iPhone only, with iOS 26 or later. The app's screens are in English and Korean, and other device languages show English. Portrait and landscape are supported. Amounts are whole numbers in your region's currency, set when you first set up the app. There are no decimals or exchange rates, so you can't enter 12.50. Recording from messages takes only payments in won.
Close the app fully, open it again, and check the App Store for the latest version. If the problem continues, email us with the screen you were on and what you were doing.

privacy.title: DailyLeft Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: The app's records are saved in a file on your device, and the developer does not receive that file. If you choose to send a message report email, the developer receives it. It is used only to teach the app that message format and to reply. It is deleted without delay after the developer decides whether to add that format to the app, and at most 1 year after it was received. Banner ads come from Google AdMob, which processes device information such as the advertising identifier.
intro: kvndh ("the developer") handles the personal information of people who use the DailyLeft app ("the app") under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act, as set out below.

sections.title: Purpose of processing
paragraphs: The app has no sign-up or login. It uses the budget and payment records you enter to work out the money left and what you can spend today. These records are in a saved file on your device, and the developer does not receive that file.
The app shows a banner ad at the bottom of the main screen. Google's ad service AdMob selects and displays that ad, and uses device information to show ads and measure how they perform.
If you send a message report email, the developer receives it. The developer uses it to teach the app that card company's message format and to reply to you, and for no other purpose.

sections.title: Information processed
paragraphs: The data the app saves on your device is listed at the end of this section. The developer does not receive it. The app does not receive contacts, location or photos.

The app can't read your Messages directly. It reads only text passed by a Shortcuts automation you made or text you paste. You decide in the Shortcuts app which messages are passed. Text that is read but not recorded is not saved. These message features appear only for the South Korea region.

If you send a message report email, the developer receives your email address, the original message text you chose to send (which may include part of the approver's name, the merchant, the card's last 4 digits, the amount and the time), the reason it could not be read, the app and iOS versions, and information your mail app adds (such as your sender name, depending on your mail account settings). The app does not send this email. You send it yourself from your own mail app, and you can delete or change it before sending.
Information that AdMob may collect when showing ads is listed in section 9.
bullets: Budget settings (budget type, currency and amount, period start day, Count weekdays only, Expires if unspent, whether payments go through over budget, how payment notices arrive, days left out in the calendar): used to work out the money left and the daily amount
Card last 4 digits (if entered): used to skip messages from other cards
Transactions (date, amount, merchant or memo, time added to the app, how it was recorded): used to work out the money left and for the transaction list

The original text of recorded payment messages: saved as is in the saved file and used so the same message isn't recorded twice. It may include part of the approver's name (for example H*D), the merchant, the card's last 4 digits, the amount and the time
The last balance seen and when, a first-run mark, the day a celebration was shown, and whether the calendar is expanded: used to draw the screen

sections.title: Processing and retention period
paragraphs: Records on your device stay until you delete them or delete the app. Delete a transaction by swiping it in the list. If no other app from the developer that uses the same App Group is on the device, deleting the app removes the records and settings with it.
A message report email is deleted without delay after the developer decides whether to add that message format to the app, and at most 1 year after it was received.
Information collected by AdMob is kept as set out in Google's Privacy Policy (policies.google.com/privacy).

sections.title: Disclosure to third parties
paragraphs: The developer does not provide users' personal information or message report emails to third parties. However, the Google Mobile Ads SDK and Google User Messaging Platform SDK built into the app send the information in section 9 directly to Google, as follows.
bullets: Recipient: Google LLC (United States), AdMob
Purpose: checking ad consent, showing ads and measuring ad performance
Information: the device information and ad interaction records listed in section 9
When and how: sent over the internet when the app opens, checks consent and starts the SDK, and when an ad is loaded and shown
Retention: as set out in Google's Privacy Policy

sections.title: Outsourcing of processing
paragraphs: The developer does not outsource the processing of personal information.
A message report email travels through your mail service to the developer's Naver mailbox (kvndh36@naver.com).

sections.title: Destruction of information
paragraphs: Records on your device are removed when you delete them from the transaction list or delete the app.
A message report email is deleted from the mailbox without delay after the developer decides whether to add that message format to the app, and at most 1 year after it was received.

sections.title: Rights of users and legal guardians, and how to exercise them
paragraphs: If you have sent a message report email, you can ask to view or delete that email at the address below. If you have questions, email us at the same address.
You can check and delete the records on your device yourself in the app.
You can ask Google to give you access to, or delete, information collected by AdMob (policies.google.com/privacy). To refuse use of the advertising identifier, follow section 9.

sections.title: Security measures
paragraphs: The app's records and settings sit in one file (ledger.json) in storage the app and its widget share on your device (an App Group). The widget only reads this file and does not use the ad SDK. Values used to draw the screen are in the app's UserDefaults. The developer runs no server, and the app does not use iCloud sync. This file can be included in iCloud or Mac backups you turn on.

The app does not send email itself. Tapping Report Message only fills in the recipient, subject and body of a mail draft, and you tap send or cancel. If no mail account is set up, it opens a mail app you choose with the same content.

The only permission the app asks for is tracking (ATT). It does not ask for photos, location, notifications, camera or contacts. The app takes clipboard text only when you paste it. Apart from ads, the only outside addresses the app opens are the message report email and this privacy policy page, and only when you tap them.
What the app passes to the ad SDK is the ad request and the banner size. It does not pass budgets, transactions, messages or card numbers.

sections.title: Automatic collection and how to refuse it
paragraphs: The app does not use cookies or analytics tools. It includes the Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob) and the Google User Messaging Platform SDK for advertising, which may collect the information below when they check ad consent and when they load and show ads. The list below is what the privacy manifests of the two SDKs declare.

The app checks ad consent information after you tap Start on the first-run screen. If you have already started, it checks when the app opens. Where ad consent is required, such as the European Economic Area, Google's consent form appears first. If ads can be requested and you haven't answered yet, iOS shows the App Tracking Transparency (ATT) prompt. If you don't allow tracking, AdMob does not get the advertising identifier (IDFA), and ads keep appearing. You can change this choice in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.
If the consent result means ads can't be requested, the tracking prompt is not shown and ads are not requested. Where consent is required, change it from Privacy Choices in Settings.
bullets: Device identifiers, and the advertising identifier (IDFA) if you allow tracking
Approximate location
Ad interaction records such as impressions and taps, and app usage records
App performance, crash and diagnostic information

sections.title: Privacy officer
paragraphs: If you have questions about personal information, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Remedies for privacy concerns
paragraphs: If you need advice about a privacy concern or help settling a dispute, you can contact the Korean bodies listed below. If you live outside Korea, you can also contact the data protection authority in your country.
bullets: Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: 1833-6972 in Korea (www.kopico.go.kr)
Personal Information Infringement Report Center: 118 in Korea (privacy.kisa.or.kr)
Supreme Prosecutors' Office: 1301 in Korea (www.spo.go.kr)
National Police Agency: 182 in Korea (ecrm.police.go.kr)
European Union and EEA: the data protection authority of your country (edpb.europa.eu)
United Kingdom: Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk)
United States: Federal Trade Commission (reportfraud.ftc.gov)
Other countries: the data protection or consumer protection authority where you live

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If this policy changes, this page will show what changed and the new effective date.
